newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy cabinet to discuss 3-yr econ plan on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Italy cabinet to discuss 3-yr econ plan on Friday.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi will present the outline of the government's latest three year economic programme (DPEF) at Friday's cabinet meeting, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said.

However, it was not clear if the eagerly-awaited document would be presented after the cabinet meeting. Government sources indicated to Reuters that the DPEF would probably be approved and officially unveiled next week.

Asked if the DPEF would include details of a planned reform of the welfare state, Treu told reporters: "There ought to be some two pages on the welfare state. We'll talk about this next week with the unions and business leaders."
Treu was talking after a meeting with Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
The DPEF will give a new deficit forecast for 1998, with the government eager to introduce structural spending cuts to enhance its credentials for membership of the planned single European currency.
Earlier on Thursday, Romualdo Coviello, chairman of the Senate's budget committee, said he expected the government to lodge the DPEF with parliament next Thursday. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
